question_text: Why should a helicopter necessarily have two propellers?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), Unit 7 VERY SHORT ANSWER. The 1+1 mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for this question, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: With one propeller

steps.margin_note: Name the law — conservation of angular momentum. That is the mark.
steps.why: The helicopter starts with zero angular momentum. If the rotor takes some in one direction, the body must take an equal amount the other way — nothing else is available to absorb it.
common_mistakes: Saying one propeller "cannot lift enough". The question is about rotation, not lift.

recall.must_convey: That with one propeller the body would rotate opposite to it, by conservation of angular momentum.
accept: the body rotates in the opposite direction

steps.memory_tip: The engine turns the rotor one way; the rotor turns the body the OTHER way. Equal, opposite torques.

steps.label: The second propeller
lines: The small tail propeller produces a

lines.text: the body of the helicopter stays steady.

steps.margin_note: Say what the tail rotor does — "counter-balances the body’s rotation" — not just that it exists.
steps.why: The tail rotor pushes air sideways, giving a torque about the main axis that cancels the reaction. That is why it sits far back on the tail — a long arm needs less force.
common_mistakes: Claiming the two propellers share the lifting. The tail rotor is for balance, not lift.

recall.must_convey: That the tail propeller supplies the balancing counter-torque so the body does not spin.
accept: second propeller stops the body rotating
reject: the body rotates in the opposite direction

steps.memory_tip: The tail rotor stands vertical and pushes air sideways. A sideways push at a long arm turns the body.

insider_note: Both marks are for naming the physics: conservation of angular momentum first, counter-torque second.
